# jawata-mcp v4.2.2

Three issues, and the thread running through them is what a writer knows about the file it is
editing. A rewrite that ignores the file's own conventions produces valid code that is wrong in
a way no compiler and no test can see — which is exactly why two of these survived a full audit
round before being found.

## A generated file is written the way the file beside it is written

`extract kind=superclass` assembles the new parent class by hand, line by line, with a literal
newline at every join. Extracting a superclass out of a file that uses Windows line endings
therefore produced a parent file that used Unix ones — measured at eleven mismatched lines on a
file of nine.

The generator now takes the delimiter from the source it is extracting from. Nothing else about
its output moves, and that is the evidence rather than a claim: the recorded parity output for
this operation is byte-identical after the change, because a file that already used Unix endings
still gets Unix endings.

**The indentation half is deliberately not fixed and is stated in the source.** The generated
members are still indented with four literal spaces, so a project that indents with tabs would
get spaces. It is left because no fixture in this suite indents with tabs, which means an
assertion about it would be satisfied by the fixture rather than by the code — and a fix nothing
can check is how the next one of these ships.

## The last rewrite that could not see the file it was editing

`data kind=add_record_component` passed no formatting options to the rewrite engine, so the
engine fell back to its own defaults rather than the file's. Every other rewrite site in the
product had already been corrected; this one was missed because the search that found them asked
the wrong question — *does this site pass a document* rather than *does this site pass options* —
and a document carries the line ending while only the options carry the indentation.

It is corrected, and the honest measurement is recorded with it: on this operation the change is
**not observable today**. Both of its edits insert text into an existing line, so it never writes
a line of its own and never asks the engine how to indent one. The correction stands because the
site would begin writing lines the moment anyone gives it a member to generate; the assertion
covering it is labelled a guard against that future rather than proof of a bug caught.

## A timeout that could not say what it failed to see

The debug-probe harness waits for a target program to reach a given class by asking the running
JVM for its stack. When that wait timed out it always reported *the target never reached its
class* — including when the harness had never managed to attach to the JVM at all, and so had no
information about the target whatsoever.

The two are now reported separately, with the count of attempts and the reason for a refused
attach. The distinction is not cosmetic: under a full four-shard test run the attach itself fails
inside its own ten-and-a-half-second window, so nothing observes the target, and the old message
made a confident claim about a program nothing had looked at.

## Also in this release

- **Eclipse workspace settings are written only when they differ.** The settings this product
  depends on are stated rather than inherited from whatever the platform defaults to; this
  release stops the common path re-writing values that already match, which was firing a
  workspace-wide change notification for nothing on every start.

Closes mcp#75. Contributes the final commit to mcp#78, which closes with this release.
